quest.title: Heart and Mind
quest.description: Skirk's strength is returning quickly but she still doesn't seem to be satisfied. She thinks something's wrong with her body and hopes to solve her problems through meditation. You arrange to see her in a couple of days. Hopefully, everything works out as planned...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... Morning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Skirk is still meditating, huh... It's been two days already! Shouldn't she be awake by now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm... Paimon can't think of anything we can do to help... Oh, wait! Breakfast! That's it! Paimon will go get breakfast! Skirk is gonna be starving when she wakes up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Be right back!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Skirk looks so serene, almost like she really is asleep...)

choices.text: Maybe it's not going too well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This place feels familiar, but where am I exactly...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There are towering cliffs, withered trees... and a strange river flowing from the horizon all the way here. But it's broken up several times along the way, with a waterfall at each break point.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (On closer inspection, the color of the water is changing. The closer I get to the lower portion, the darker it becomes. Almost as if...)

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: That's right! This is Skirk's inner world. Think of it as the threshold between the soul and dreams.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: This isn't your first time here, but what you remember is probably a space covered in darkness. I only managed to illuminate a small portion for you back then.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Hehe, actually, it's my first time talking to someone like this.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: I only managed to break free and bring you here because the injury weakened her power. I guess that's why I can speak again, too.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Call it "fate" if you want. I think that's the word they use in this world for lucky coincidences like this, right?

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Now, before I take you to her, I gotta ask... You're the first outside visitor to ever come here. So, what's your impression of this place?

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Ah, you noticed.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: This river represents Skirk's strength.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Strength accumulates over time. It is the summation of a person's lived experience. So, this river is where all the fragments of Skirk's life should converge into a single stream of memories and emotions, flowing forward as one.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: But, as you can see, this river has been severed numerous times... It's because Skirk doesn't like who she was in the past.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: When all she sees reflected in the river is a disgraceful shadow of who she was, she cuts through water and rock with the sword of "reason," severs her connection with the past, and begins anew.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, that reminds me of something...)

response.speaker: Surtalogi
response.text: You must learn to shut out all the pointless emotion, crush the self that makes you weak, and become master over your physical form.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: This isn't my first taste of failure or losing power. When you fall, you get back up again and become stronger, that's how it is.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I see. So, it was Surtalogi who taught Skirk to replace all emotion with reason.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And since then, it's been a constant process of abandoning, refuting, and erasing her past self. I suppose that's the secret to her strength...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But... it's such a sad thing to think about. What has she been through? Why does it have to be this way?)

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: The answer to one mystery invites another question, I see.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Let's follow the river upstream. There among the cliffs, among the memories etched into her heart, lies the truth of it all. Soon, you'll understand everything.

choices.text: Why are there so many cliffs and waterfalls?
Then, that must mean this is...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This looks like a coastline. Huh, I recognize the drawing on the sand...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait... Isn't that the picture I drew for Paimon? Why is it showing up in Skirk's memories?)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: I've always thought that, even when falling leaves don't come from the same tree, they can still form bonds of kinship when they meet.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Like meteors, you both made a journey through the stars — both travelers who have landed on a planet that is not your home. Yet, when she first noticed your presence, although she hesitated for a moment, she still chose to walk away, indifferent as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hmm... If I think about it, it's not surprising at all. After what happened at Wanmin Restaurant, it's obvious she prefers to disappear from other people's lives.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She hasn't seen Childe in years, either... I doubt she's ever made a connection with this world of her own volition. What I'm seeing now is a microcosm of her entire life.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Seems like you've answered your own question.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Skirk sees herself as a trespasser in this world. She's made a conscious choice to avoid altering its path. But, the reason for that decision stems from events much earlier on in her life.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Let's keep going. It's still a long way to the source of the river.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You now have what it takes to wield immense power. From this day forth, I shall teach you no more.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: No one can become a worthy warrior through imitation alone. I have given you fangs and claws — now, you must learn to hunt.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You wish me to travel the world beyond on my own, Master?

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Indeed. Make new friends, embark on your own journey, and piece together a new future from the shattered remnants of your past.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: We will still have contact through the Abyss. But know this: One day, I will take the life you work so hard to rebuild and reduce it to ashes — just like the "fire" that haunts your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Why... would you do that?

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: I have told you before. Fear is the catalyst for human evolution.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You have tasted loss. You have known fear so deep it can be felt in the bones.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: But, as living beings, we all have an instinct to detach from that which harms us. And, thus, pain dampens over time, and the acrid taste of fear becomes but a distant memory.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Yet now, I have bestowed upon you the gift of fear eternal. It will drown you in the nightmare of your childhood, or it shall drive you to defeat me whatever the cost.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That figure next to Skirk looks familiar. Right! I saw the same figure during the battle against the All-Devouring Narwhal...)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: That is what Skirk's master, "The Foul" Surtalogi, looked like at one point in time.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Of course. As a higher being, physical form is a triviality to him.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: He could appear as a beast, a human, or even a monster that defies description. The form you see him in here, clad in Abyssal armor, is the one he usually wears when traveling through the stars.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I used to think Surtalogi and Skirk were just master and disciple, like Skirk and Childe.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Now, I see why Skirk chose to distance herself from humanity. Surtalogi told her to put down roots here, while at the same time threatening to destroy whatever life she managed to create.)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: For certain reasons, I need to bridge the power gap between me and my master as quickly as possible. But, first, I need to understand the source of his strength.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: To do that, I need to follow in his footsteps, walk the path he once walked. And somewhere along the way, I'll find out how to defeat him. That is my sole focus and purpose.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So, that's what she meant. But, I still don't understand why Surtalogi would do that. From what he said, I didn't pick up on a conflict between them.)

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: I'll let you in on a little secret — the real Surtalogi is terrifying.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: The scope of his power is impossible to understand until you experience it first-hand. It is absolute — the power to crush all things.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Shall we keep going? Let's see... we're about halfway there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This must be Skirk when she was a kid.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: We've made it quite a ways already! This is Skirk when she first began training under Surtalogi.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: I have set your broken wrist. Tomorrow, you're to train twice as hard.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: No tears this time... Good. Attempting to garner sympathy through tears is a habit of the weak — a pitiful, useless ploy.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Can I ask a question, Master? Why did you save me?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I keep thinking... maybe it would be better if I had died. I wouldn't be haunted by that fire all the time. I wouldn't have to go on like this...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: I saved you because I have a plan for you.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: It has been too long since I fought a battle that demanded my full strength, and I hunger for it. Every so-called genius and prodigy I have faced has crumbled like sand underfoot. Before me, even fate bends the knee.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: So, I will teach you everything I know, train you by whatever means necessary... In the hope that, one day, you might surprise me.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: But, I don't want to draw my sword against you, Master!

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: What you want matters little.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Among the boundless sea of stars, the cries of the weak are but faint murmurs that disappear into the void. You of all people know that well.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Yes, Master.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: From that day forward, all she knew was grueling training, emptiness, and fatigue.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: After some time, her talent bloomed, and she gained control over her emotions like her master. Uh, how should I put it...

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: It was not that human emotion disappeared from her heart, but that reason came to dictate all she was allowed to feel. I suppose it was at this point that she became the Skirk you know today.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, Surtalogi saved Skirk from a disaster when she was a child and never even tried to hide his ulterior motive.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I suppose that leaves one final mystery... What really happened with the disaster back then?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Surtalogi's final words to Skirk were cold and cruel. But, Skirk's reaction made it seem like it was a truth she knew all too well. I have a feeling it all comes back to what happened back then.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Ah... We're nearly there!

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: I almost don't want to reach the end... Well, shall we? This is the final stretch.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Ah... These are Skirk's happiest memories.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: What a simple and carefree time it was — wisps of clouds dotted the sky, the sun bathed everything in golden light. And when song filled the air, not even the shyest of flowers could resist swaying along.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: This is Skirk's homeland. She was so curious about everything as a child, always skipping school to go exploring instead.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: There was so much to discover — the treasures at the bottom of the sea, the secrets beyond the stars, and that "merchant ship" packed with adults wearing those strange clothes... Yes, the ship. That was the beginning of the end.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: It was a spaceship. When it arrived, the people that disembarked wore smiles on their faces and spoke of friendship. They claimed to be merchants from a neighboring planet looking to establish trade.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Skirk's parents, her relatives, her neighbors... Everyone welcomed the newcomers with open arms and allowed them to explore the planet. To them, the visitors were guests and should be treated with hospitality.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: No one had any idea of what was to come. Several months later, an army of unknown origin arrived without warning and carried out a ruthless campaign to destroy everything, and everyone, on the planet.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Skirk had skipped school that day, like so many times before, so she was not caught in the immediate wave of destruction. But, when she came home that day, only fire and ruin awaited her.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Countless people cried out to her for help, people she knew and loved — friends and relatives, the little girl who lived next-door, the shop-owner with the bad leg, the bad-tempered teacher she had made fun of just that morning...

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: Their lives were discarded like worthless trash. As the fire consumed one life after another, Skirk was helpless. All she could do was run. And so she did. She kept running until an unexpected figure crossed her path.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: If Surtalogi hadn't been there in that moment, the fire would have claimed her life too. And there she would have remained, left to rot in the scorched earth, with no answer as to why any of this was happening.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Because she and her people were seen as a "threat."

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: As the initial merchant ship explored the planet, they discovered that it hadn't always had the condition to support life. Yet, there was evidence of human activity even during the periods of extreme heat or cold in the past.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Further research revealed that, over time, the people of this planet had evolved the ability to adapt to any type of environment or energy source.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: For that reason, the outsiders viewed them as a "potential threat," and decided to eliminate them before the threat could rear its head. And so, the army was called, and the so-called danger was wiped from the face of the planet.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Senseless, isn't it? Deemed a threat because of a gift they didn't even know they had. Perhaps it was their own innocence and kindness that doomed them. But, in the end, that was lost to the blaze as well.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: If those with power get to decide good and evil, then all you can trust in is the sword in your hand. And so, before death could claim her, she ran. She ran and never stopped.

choices.text: Now I see why Surtalogi's threat is such a terrifying prospect for her.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: No one wants to relive their most painful moments... Well, that brings us to the end of the story. This is as far as we can go.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Skirk is waiting over there... for both of us.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Let's go to her. It's time to fulfill my purpose... and my greatest wish over all these years.

choices.text: And now I see why she distances herself from the world.
Why did those people destroy her homeland?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: #So, all this, just so you could bring {M#him}{F#her} here?

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: I have things to say to "you"... Well, to "me."

dialogues.speaker: Strange Creature
dialogues.text: #I want someone to witness our reconciliation, even if it takes an argument to get there. And, {M#he}{F#she} is the best choice in this moment.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Her suppressed emotional self. The version of herself she keeps locked in the recesses of her mind, stifled by reason.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: All those rejected impulses, those discarded aspects of your past selves... They are a part of me now.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: I am who you used to be, someone you have refused to face for too long. So, I came to face you instead.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You're wrong. I've faced you all along, and that's exactly why I keep you locked here.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Your existence makes me weak. Moments of joy and longing are when we are most vulnerable.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Don't forget, it was a penchant for goodness over reason that doomed our homeland in the first place. The vastness of the universe renders everything insignificant, our feelings most of all.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Even so, learning from the mistakes of the past doesn't have to mean erasing everything.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Strip yourself of your so-called weaknesses — emotions like kindness and empathy — and what makes you any different from the ruthless soldiers who slaughtered our people?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: The difference is that I'm doing what is right — what is necessary.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I allow you to exist, but with limited freedom. That is the greatest kindness I can offer.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I've shouldered everything you couldn't carry. I rose above the numbness and emptiness, and it was cold, unfeeling reason that brought me this far. It made me who I am. It made me strong.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: That is the problem. I want to shoulder those things together.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: On the grand scale of the entire universe, maybe our feelings are vanishingly small, but why should that mean they don't matter? Emotion gives warmth to the cold expanse of space. It gives meaning to the world around us.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Think back to those nights of gazing at the stars, those afternoons of exploring the unknown. Think back and let them grant you peace, a brief respite from the pressure you put on yourself.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That isn't what we need.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: It's exactly what we need!

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Aren't you curious about why recovering your strength has taken longer than normal this time?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Finally, you get to the important part. That is the only answer I came here to find.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Then, look around. Look at your inner world.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: You cast aside your dreams and curiosity, and in doing so you lost your original motivation. You severed all connection to who you used to be, so you can no longer draw strength from your past.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Now, the only things driving you forward are fear and survivor's guilt, but these cannot take you far enough. And so, this river — the source of your strength — grows more polluted by the day.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: And you think that means I should seek help from a weak little thing like you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Your emotional self isn't weak.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The fact that she transcended time and broke free from her constraints to come and face you... That proves it.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Thank you for saying that. I knew bringing you here would be the right choice.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: To be honest, I'm not here to argue with you. This isn't about who's right or wrong. And in fact, I agree that in order to make it through the wake of that tragedy, we had to distance ourselves from the pain through reason over emotion.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: But, what is right at one point in time isn't always right forever. I know you will never forget that fire. I know the fact that you were the sole survivor fills you with guilt.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: And I know that among the voices that haunt you, mine is there too. Because deep down, you know that you didn't turn out to be the person you wanted to be.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: All those unfulfilled hopes are like knives to the heart, and I don't want you to hurt anymore. So, even if you can't accept me, I hope, at least... that you can let go.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I remember, there was a song Mom and Dad always sang when we went out to fetch water.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: "Dancing water, the sand along your path is begging for your song and movement. Will you carry this burden with you on your journey?"

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I am not the dancing water, and you are not the burdensome sand. But, if this is your wish... then I will carry you with me until the end.

response.speaker: Strange Creature
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...I should be thanking you.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: So, you saw my memories then...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I once asked my master if "survival of the strongest" was the law of the universe.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: He said no, "but in a world without order, those with no moral boundaries tend to be the ones who survive."

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That's why, after hearing his answer, an idea came to mind.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: An idea that, one day, I would create a new world order, one in which there would never be another tragedy like that fire. One in which power was not the law of the land.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But, that means I must defeat him. Because my master, Surtalogi, is, at the core, a defier of all rules and order.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like you have your work cut out for you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Yes, and not just because of the gap in our abilities, but also because... I have no reason to see him as an enemy.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Although his decision to train me was not made out of kindness, he did everything a master should. He saved my life, taught me the sword and the principles of strength... And, for that, I respect him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, he intends to face you in battle one day...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I know, and it's not something I want. But, Master never goes back on his word. I have to treat everything he says as a promise.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: He's no longer in Teyvat, but he sends me messages through the Abyss every now and then. Most of them are simple greetings, or an answer to one of my questions.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Every time I hear from him, my heart skips a beat, and I wonder if this is the moment where he'll finally appear before me and tear down everything I've built to pieces.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Maybe that means I do live in eternal fear, just like he said. Yes, I respect him, but I'm also afraid of him. And, for that reason, the pursuit of strength consumes every moment of my life.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I don't know what Master has planned, but I have to be ready.

choices.text: If he does attack you one day...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Help me...? Why? This isn't your fight.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because if we want to build the world we both want to see... everyone has to be willing to fight for it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If we all do our part, we can make the entire universe a kinder place.

choices.text: Power is not a substitute for doing what is right.

talks.objective: Exit the threshold between the soul and dreams

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Skirk gazes into the distant sky.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's nothing else to do here. Should I leave?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you're finally awake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Honestly, Paimon was gone for, like, two seconds, and then she comes back and finds you both unconscious? You scared Paimon half to death!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're both okay, right?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: What does it look like?

choices.text: Looks like your strength is back.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Only water from the source can cleanse the rot and filth that flows from the past into the future.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I taught you to incorporate the experiences from your journey into how you fight. I suppose what happened today... will become an inseparable part of who I am.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so Paimon feels like she's missing some important context...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, whatever. Paimon brought back tons of delicious snacks! Let's dig in!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The three of you enjoy the snacks...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Alright, it's about time we finished what we started.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're gonna deal with this thief for good, right?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: This time, I'm not going to tell you to hold back. But, having digested even more power in the meantime, he's going to be tougher than before.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: The good news is, we have no reason to pull our punches this time. So, let's go. Same place as last time.

choices.text: Let's show him what we're made of!

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: (I'm sick of being a kid... There's so many amazing things out there, and I'm ready to see them all!)

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Your dad and I, we're not afraid to stare death in the face. But, we need you to survive.
